To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in a harmonically trapped two dimensional optical lattice the superfluid order-parameter and the density of unpared fermions exhibit a transition from single peak to double peak as the imbalance increases from low to high values.

the ground state of the attractive Fermi Hubbard model with harmonic trapping is characterized by a modulated order parameter that depends on the imbalance, density and trapping frequency, and leads to a double peak in the density profile of the unpaired fermion for an intermediate imbalance, but leads single peaks for low and high imbalances.

population imbalanced fermions in a harmonically trapped optical lattice can have double peaks in their density profile, with one peak at the center of the trap and the other at the trap edges, for intermediate imbalance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ground state phase diagram of harmonically trapped two dimensional optical lattice systems of population imbalanced Fermi mixtures in the attractive regime.
the ground state properties of a mixture of two-component fermions with population imbalance in a 2D optical lattice, and the effect of the trap potential.
the physics of ultracold fermion mixtures trapped in optical lattices, and the effect of population imbalance on the ground state phase of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superfluid to superfluid phase transition is a first order transition for low imbalance, and is a continuous transition for high imbalance.
the superfluid order parameters modulates towards the center of the trap with low density and low population imbalance.

the ground state of the attractive Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonian in a harmonically trapped optical lattice is a superfluid with a spatially modulating order parameter and a single peak in its density profile for low imbalance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unpaired fermion density profile is a sensitive probe for the superfluid order in harmonically trapped fermionic mixtures.

in the low density limit a single peak in unpaired fermion density is always found for any imbalance while in the high density regime the density of unpared fermions has a single or double peak depending on the value of the imbalance.

in the high density regime the order parameter modulations are driven by the imbalance and not by the trap potential, while the trap potential dominates the order parameter modulation in the low density regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the density profile of the unpaired fermion species is sensitive to the population imbalance and density of the mixture.

the superfluid order parameters of the two species can have opposite modulations in the radial direction for a given imbalance and the density profiles of unpaired fermionic species can have single or double peaks depending upon the imbalance.
in addition to the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, there is also a superfluid to normal transition with increasing imbalance.
